subject: Prioritization: CentraBank enterprise pilot — tenant routing SLA and observability hooks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@centrabank.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@centrabank.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Prioritization: CentraBank enterprise pilot — tenant routing SLA and observability hooks

Team,

CentraBank is ready to move from evaluation -> pilot, but procurement has one gating ask that we need engineering/product alignment on before they sign: tenant-level routing guarantees (isolation of noisy tenants) and an SLA window for 99th p99 latency for their high-priority traffic. They also want richer per-tenant observability hooks (trace id propagation + per-tenant tokenized cost reporting) exposed during the pilot.

I've attached a short requirements doc (centra_mvp_requirements.pdf) and their initial SLA draft (sla-draft-centrabank.docx). High-level asks: 
- Tenant routing policy with prioritized lanes for 2 critical services (authentication & payments)
- 99th percentile latency goal: <= 450ms for prioritized lane at our expected load
- Trace-id passthrough + per-tenant metrics to feed their splunk

They need an implementation timeline and clarity on permanence (pilot -> GA). Procurement wants to know whether this is a product change (long runway) or a short-term configuration/shim we can promise for Q1. Can you (Rishi/Dev/Markus/Hannah) tell me what prioritization and timeline looks like so I can put a firm milestone in the SOW?

Thanks — Marissa

Attachments: centra_mvp_requirements.pdf (application/pdf), sla-draft-centrabank.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@centrabank.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@centrabank.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prioritization: CentraBank enterprise pilot — tenant routing SLA and observability hooks

Thanks Marissa. Quick responses and ask list so product/eng can scope: 

1) Customer numbers: what steady-state QPS and concurrent sessions do they expect on the prioritized lane? Are the prioritized flows short-lived API calls or long-running context streams?
2) Observability: do they require us to push metrics into their Splunk instance (push) or provide per-tenant metrics endpoints/exports (pull)?
3) Permanence: is this required only for the pilot (90 days) or will they require this as a GA feature? That affects implementation approach.

From product constraints: adding a tenant-routing primitive and exposing per-tenant metrics can be done two ways — a short-term config/shim that maps tenant IDs to an internal priority lane + metrics tagging, or a longer-term product change with routing policies in the control plane. Dev/Markus: initial engineering estimates please (spike/implement). Hannah — can you confirm commercial ask (SOW language) and whether CentraBank will accept an interim support commitment?

If we can get answers today I’ll spin up a quick prioritization note for PLG/product.

— Rishi

Hi all,

Quick answers from our side to help scoping: 
- Prioritized flows are short RPC calls (auth, payment verification). Expected peak QPS on prioritized lane: 850 QPS with sustained bursts to 1.2k QPS during market open.
- Average payloads are small (~200 tokens). Latency sensitivity is high for payments.
- Observability: preferred is that Redwood push per-tenant metrics and traces to our Splunk ingestion endpoint (we can provide tokens). Pull endpoints are less desirable.
- Commitment: Procurement will sign the pilot SOW if the pilot includes the routing shim + an agreed canary window and a 90-day pilot SLA. GA requirement TBD upon pilot success.

Procurement also attached our timeline and internal approval dates — see procurement_timeline.pdf. We can join a technical call Thursday to walk the flows.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachments: procurement_timeline.pdf (application/pdf)

Subject: Re: Prioritization: CentraBank enterprise pilot — tenant routing SLA and observability hooks

Thanks for the context — a few engineering notes from a feasibility perspective: 

- Short-term approach (pilot-friendly): implement a routing-shim in the request router that maps CentraBank tenant IDs to a high-priority execution lane. Add token-based tagging to every request so per-tenant metrics are emitted by the runtime. Exporter: implement a Splunk HTTP exporter that will push aggregated per-tenant metrics and traces. Estimated work: 1-week spike to validate, then 4 weeks to implement and test (total ~5 weeks).

- Production/GA approach: add a control-plane routing policy entity and end-to-end billing/metrics support. This is a larger product change (8–12 weeks).

- Risk: priority lane reduces noisy neighbor risk but does not guarantee absolute isolation if underlying GPU capacity saturates. For strict guaranteed isolation we'd need capacity reservation (Dedicated) work; that's a separate ask.

- Operational ask: need an SLO guardrail for burst traffic and a clear throttling policy. I recommend we accept pilot SLA for 90 days with an agreed burst throttle and fallbacks (failover to standard lane) if capacity is threatened.

I can run the spike starting next week if leadership marks this as priority. Draft design notes attached (routing-shim-design-notes.md).

— Dev
